analysis:
Examined the head text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 1-997) and the patch ranges. The visible change is in the media-through-v2 path (head lines ~789-799 and 821-823). It computes a `reasoningPrefix` from the rendered media prompt tail (ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix, falling back to contentSeed). That prefix is passed as `stopStringScope: ReasoningStopScope.scope(...)` to bridge.submitTokenized, and the same value is reused in makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream. The old inline computation at roughly base 825-836 was removed, so the stream builder now uses the earlier value.

Security-relevant observations:
- No change to cache scoping. cacheScope, cacheEnabled and mediaPrefixIdentity are unchanged, so T-041 cache isolation is unaffected.
- No change to the release/fire paths. The new code sits inside the existing do/catch at line 729, which releases mediaGate and releaseBox on throw. The decode closure is non-throwing.
- Tokenizer decoding of the prompt tail happens locally. No prompt content is logged or exposed, and the promptPrep logger carries metadata only.
- Reasoning/stop-string scoping affects only output classification and stop handling. It does not touch the encryption, attestation or authorization boundaries.

Unverified points for integration: the implementation of ReasoningStopScope.scope and the new stopStringScope parameter of submitTokenized is outside the supplied evidence. The tail of the patch, with the removed lines near base 1422 and head 1426-1428, is truncated and not visible. I did not verify whether stop-string leakage could occur when the scope is wrong. No concrete regression is identified.
